perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s perspective, I know/observed/heard/did:

- I am a Speech-Language Pathologist. Shirley Whiteplume is a nurse, a long-time colleague, and a close friend at our community health center.
- I attended the funeral of a patient we both cared for. I saw Shirley was somber and suspected she was deeply affected. I told her I knew it was hard and that I had seen how much she cared.
- I heard Shirley say it had been tough, that she kept thinking something more could have been done, and that it was hard to let go. I told her we did everything we could and should remember the good care and joy we brought the patient.
- During a coffee break at work, I brought up our treatment decisions because I sensed Shirley felt burdened. I heard her say she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. I told her we made the best decisions with the information we had and that she should not carry the burden alone. She thanked me and said it was hard to accept.
- In a quiet moment in our office, I noticed Shirley had been reserved and showed little emotion. I told her she was holding back and that it was okay to be open. I heard her say she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. I said showing emotion is not weak and is healthy among friends. She said maybe I was right and she would try.
- I later felt I might have come on too strong, so I apologized. Shirley said it had been a bit much but that she knew I meant well and appreciated the apology. I told her I was there for her however she needed. She thanked me and said talking helps.
- Later, I noticed Shirley seemed improved. I asked how she felt. She said she was better thanks to our talks and my support. I suggested spending more time together outside work. She agreed, and we planned something for the weekend.

I do not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she said or what I observed.
